subject: Analytics vendor consolidation — options, timeline, and decision path
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.com, marcus.lin@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Cc: tessa.morgan@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Analytics vendor consolidation — options and timeline

Team,

Quick primer: we have three overlapping contracts in Q4–Q1 that touch inference telemetry and product analytics: Segment (CDP / event routing), Amplitude (product analytics), Mixpanel (product + API analytics pilot). Rather than renew all three independently, I want us to evaluate a consolidation path (one primary analytics vendor + event routing retained/retired) versus best-of-breed (keep specialized tools).

Key constraints:
- Contract renewal milestones: Segment renewal 2026-12-15; Amplitude amendment renewal 2027-01-10; Mixpanel pilot ends 2026-12-31.
- Data residency & SOC2: legal needs a short evidence packet for any vendor we recommend.
- Traffic shape: 1.8B events/mo across prod APIs and product events; median event size ~800 bytes; 99th p50 latency requirement for realtime funnels ~200ms.

Asks this week:
1) Review attached procurement-rfp-analytics.docx and add gaps/risks.
2) Fill the compare-sheet (attached) with observed query patterns, downstream consumers, and retention requirements.
3) Flag any migration blockers (e.g., schema incompatibilities, ingestion cost).

Goal: internal recommendation by 2026-11-10 so procurement can lock pricing and legal can prepare SOC2 addenda if needed.

Thanks — Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Senior Product Manager, Instrumentation
Redwood Inference

Attachments: procurement-rfp-analytics.docx, compare-sheet-analytics-vendors.xlsx
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 21 Oct 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Analytics vendor consolidation — options and timeline

Dylan —

Thanks for the summary. A few quick notes after a first pass of the compare sheet:
- Event volume spikes from batch jobs (nightly ingestion) currently cause undifferentiated egress spikes that materially increase Segment costs. We should quantify monthly ingest vs API calls.
- Retention: legal wants 13 months of raw event retention for auditability; Amplitude charges more for long-term raw exports.
- Technical debt: our sessionization and device attributes are implemented as downstream transforms in Segment today; fully moving to an analytics-only vendor will require 3–4 weeks of engineering migration work (schema mapping + replay).

Propose a 45-min sync Thursday to surface blockers and finalize the vendor questions list.

— Marcus
Director, Observability Engineering

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, marcus.lin@redwood.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 25 Oct 2026 08:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Analytics vendor consolidation — options and timeline

Dylan/Marcus —

Legal/procurement pull: we need vendor SOC2 attestations (Type II preferred), standard DPA language, and clarity on subprocessor lists before we can commit to long-term deals. If we consolidate to a single vendor, procurement will require a risk memo addressing:
- Data residency guarantees and export controls
- SLA credits for query latency / ingestion failures
- Right-to-audit & breach notification timelines

Cost note: I pulled last quarter's invoices. If we scale Amplitude to cover both product analytics + API analytics ingestion, list price looks better but we should insist on committed ingestion blocks or tiered ETL credits — otherwise egress/ingest can spike costs unexpectedly.

I'll compile a vendor evidence checklist and drop it in the Drive.

— Laura
Head of Procurement

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Tran <sophie.tran@amplitude.com>, Raj Malhotra <raj@mixpanel.com>, sales@segment.com
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com, marcus.lin@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com, tessa.morgan@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 30 Oct 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Request for updated SOWs & migration notes — Redwood Inference analytics evaluation

Hi Sophie / Raj / Segment team —

Redwood is running a short vendor evaluation across Amplitude, Mixpanel, and Segment to decide on an analytics model for product + API telemetry. We are comparing three paths: consolidate analytics into one vendor, split ingestion/routing from analytics, or continue best-of-breed.

Requested deliverables (response by 2026-11-06 if possible):
- Updated SOW or proposal tailored to 2B events/month, 13 months retention, and cross-region replication to EU.
- Migration notes: recommended approach to replay historical events, schema compatibility, recommended SDKs, and estimated eng hours.
- Security evidence: SOC2 Type II, subprocessor list, encryption at-rest keys, and DPA template.
- Pricing model examples: committed ingestion vs overage, query cost model, and volume discounts.

Please attach native PDFs. Laura (procurement) is cc'd for contract items. If you'd prefer a short call, happy to schedule next week.

Thanks,
Dylan

From: Sophie Tran <sophie.tran@amplitude.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Cc: marcus.lin@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 14:28:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request for updated SOWs & migration notes — Redwood Inference analytics evaluation

Dylan —

Thanks for the note and the detailed ask. Attached is our initial outbound proposal (Amplitude_Enterprise_5yr_proposal.pdf) and a short migration playbook (SOW_amplitude_trial.pdf). High level:
- We can support 2B events/mo with committed ingestion blocks and a staged migration approach to reduce overage risk.
- Retention: we offer raw event exports and long-term retention; will include options for 13/24-month retention tiers.
- Security: attached SOC2 Type II summary and subprocessor list. Full artifacts available under NDA — happy to coordinate with Laura.

A few open items for us to scope:
1) How many distinct event types do you send today?
2) Do you require realtime API-level funneling for infra metrics (we saw mention of 200ms p50)?

Happy to hop on a call with the team this week; propose Wed 11/4 or Thu 11/5.

Best,
Sophie Tran
Enterprise Sales, Amplitude

Attachments: Amplitude_Enterprise_5yr_proposal.pdf, SOW_amplitude_trial.pdf, amplitude-soc2-summary.pdf
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.com, marcus.lin@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com, tessa.morgan@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 15:45:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Analytics vendor consolidation — options, timeline, and decision path

Team — quick internal recap after vendor replies: 

- Amplitude returned a formal proposal (attached). They can scale to 2B events/mo with committed ingestion blocks and offered migration support; they flagged realtime funneling as an item to validate (see Sophie's questions).
- Mixpanel (Raj) indicated willingness to bid to consolidate product & API analytics but asked for detailed query samples — I flagged the compare-sheet.
- Segment responded with options to continue as CDP-only (keep routing) or expand to more advanced transforms; pricing TBD.

Recommendation: shortlist Amplitude + Mixpanel for detailed costing and migration timelines. The primary tradeoffs by path are:
- Consolidate on Amplitude: lower operational surface, single vendor SLA, likely higher one-time migration lift.
- Best-of-breed (Segment + Mixpanel): lower migration lift, better event routing control, potentially higher ongoing cost and duplicate storage.

Immediate asks:
1) Laura — please confirm whether procurement can accept Amplitude's NDA to surface full SOC2 artifacts and proceed to a term sheet if pricing is reasonable.
2) Marcus & Marissa — please validate the realtime funneling requirement (200ms p50) against Amplitude's architecture and provide a thumbs-up / red-flag by EOD Thu 11/11.
3) I'll schedule a 1-hour decision sync for 11/12 to finalize the direction.

Forwarding Sophie's message below for context.

-----Original Message-----
